newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Co
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- OFWAT DEMANDS 50 POUNDS OFF WATER BILLS

Ofwat, the water industry watchdog, has made proposals to the government that would mean that up to a fifth of Britain's homes stand to have their water bills cut by up to 50 pounds a year. The price cut is being called for by Ofwat as a condition of allowing the bid battle for South West Water to proceed.
-- KINGFISHER SET TO SWOOP ON NORWEB.

Kingfisher, the stores giant, is in the early stages of negotiations with United Utilities over the acquisition of the electric retail operations of Norweb. United Utilities hopes to sell the 70 out-of town-superstores and 60 shops for 70 million stg, and a trade sale to Kingfisher, which owns the comet retail chain, seems most likely.
-- BASE RATE PRESSURE MOUNTS ON CLARKE

The prospect of an interest rate rise before the May general election is looking more likely as fears that the domestic economy is set to overheat. Treasury insiders are concerned about house prices while figures out last week showed a 15.5 percent rise in outstanding consumer credit, the fastest rate of increase since 1989.
-- MANPOWER TO DROP LONDON LISTING

The world's largest employment agency is to cancel its London listing. Manpower, formerly the Blue Arrow group, has decided that its London listing is now no longer needed as almost all its shares are traded in the U.S.
-- ORANGE LAUNCHES VISA CREDIT CARD

Orange, the mobile phone company, is to launch the Orange Visa Card, this weekend. The credit and global calling card will be offered to the 660,000 subscribers to Orange through a link-up with NatWest. The card offers 56 days of interest free credit and a competitive interest rate provided holders spend over 1,800 pounds.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- MAID UNDERCUTS REUTERS WITH CUSTOMISED NEWS

Dan Wagner's Maid group is planning an assault on the leaders of the electronic information industry, Reuters and Bloomberg, through the launch of real-time financial news services. The planned package of products is thought to include a screen-based real-time information service that will sharply undercut the existing services from Reuters and Bloomberg, as well as the transmission of data to hand-held devices.
-- HYUNDAI SCOTTISH PLANT TO BE GIVEN 150 MLN POUNDS AID

The government is expected to announce a 150 million stg aid package for the proposed Hyundai microchip-manufacturing facilities in Dunfermline, Fife in Scotland. Michael Forsyth, the Scottish secretary, is likely to unveil the inward investment project during his speech on Tuesday to the Tory party conference.
-- BROWN 'WILL INTRODUCE AUSTERITY BUDGET'

According to a forecast the Labour government would be forced to introduce an austerity budget and raise base rates. The Forecast, to be published this week by the Independent Treasury Economic Modellers, Gordon Brown would be forced to raise base rates to 7 percent from 5.75 percent now to curb rising inflation and introduce a tough budgeT, due to the state of the public finances.
-- ASHWORTH PUTS 25 MLN STG FLOAT IN THE PIPELINE

Oliver Ashworth, a leading British pipeline distributor, is planning a 25 million stg flotation next month. The Manchester based company will raise 10 million stg to pay back its venture-capital backers and fund expansion.
-- THOMSON SALE WILL SHAKE UK DEFENCE

The Lagardere group will aim to form joint ventures with UK companies if it wins the battle to buy Thomson, the French government owned electronics group. The UK companies that may be involved in joint ventures include British Aerospace, General Electric Co and Smiths Industries.
THE OBSERVER
-- NUCLEAR GROUP TO MAKE JOB AND COST CUTS OFFICIAL

British Energy are expected to confirm a 100 million stg cost-cutting programme this week, that will lead to the shedding of up to 25 percent of its workforce by the end of the decade. The loss of up to 1,500 jobs is likely to raise safety fears.
-- MINIMUM WAGE 'NEED NOT BE FEARED'

A study published by the Economic & Social Research Council suggests that the economy may not suffer as much as feared from the effects of a national minimum wage. The report says that the impact on costs, jobs and inflation will depend on the level at which a minimum wage is set, it suggests that there may be only a limited second round effect as people demand more money to maintain differentials.
-- BUYERS JOSTLE FOR LONRHO HOTEL CHAINS

Lonrho will decide on the buyers for its Princess and Metropole hotel chain this week. International businesses with interests outside the hotel world are expected to bid for the Princess chain which is to be sold within the next four weeks for between 650 and 700 million stg.
-- LONDON ZOO GOES FISHING FOR FUNDING FOR NATIONAL AQUARIUM

The Zoological society of London is planning the first 'probono' (for the public good) bond issue in Britain. It hopes to raise funds for a national aquarium in London's Docklands. It intends to issue 45 million stg of bonds in the US to finance the national aquarium which will cost 90 million stg.
-- MYSTERY OF YOUNG AND THE $5 MLN ISSUE

Ashurst Technology, a high tech company invested by Peter Young, the sacked Morgan Grenfell fund manager, has been unable to discover all the real owners of a $5 million debenture issue. The issue was handled by London broker Fiba Nordic Securities in February.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- US TURNS UP HEAT ON BA

USAir is to put increased pressure on British Airways to resolve the dispute between the two airlines. It will outline details of widespread US political support for its ambitions to participate in a liberated transatlantic air travel regime. It is believe in the US that BA will have to settle its differences with USAir before a deal can be approved with American Airlines.
-- DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL MAY SUE FUND AUDITORS AND TRUSTEES

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell may take legal action against the auditors and trustees of the three unit trusts formerly managed by Peter Young. DMG will scrutinise the role of the auditors KPMG and General Accident once it has completed investigations into the three trusts.
-- OUTSIDERS VITAL TO GAS INQUIRY

Ofgas has said that evidence from external advisers used over its pricing proposals for TransCo, British Gas's pipeline business, could prove crucial in the forthcoming inquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
-- TUNNEL INVESTORS READY FOR COURT

Bankruptcy proceedings will be started against Eurotunnel as French shareholders feel the debt-for-equity rescue deal is not adequate. The package to be announced tomorrow may cause a significant fall in Eurotunnel's share price on Tuesday which could trigger such action.
-- RETAILERS ATTACK EUROPEAN MOVE TOWARDS TWO-YEAR GUARANTEES

New legislation to improve guarantees on consumer goods from the European Union has been criticised by the Confederation of British Industry, the British Retail Consortium and the Consumers' Association who claim the draft directive is unworkable, environmentally unsafe.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- NORWICH UNION IN WINDFALL SCANDAL

A leading branch of Norwich Union has been encouraging financial advisers fraudulently to backdate new policy proposal forms to beat the bonanza's cut-off date. New policies had to be taken out by the end of Tuesday, October 1 to qualify for the bonus. The Financial Mail has been received information suggesting that one office was contacting advisers after the deadline and recommending that advisers backdate proposal forms.
-- ABBEY ACTION OVER BUNGLING

Abbey National is reviewing the way it dealt with the complaints arising from its 1.4 billion stg takeover of National & Provincial building society. The move has been ordered by deputy executive Charles Toner and follows the bungles by its Bradford share information office.
-- FAYEDS LOOK AT SHARE SPLIT

The Fayed brothers are considering a controversial two-tier share structure for the 2.0 billion stg flotation of their West London department store, Harrods. The move would created two types of shares but only one type would have voting rights and these shares would be held by the Fayeds.
-- PIZZA CHAIN SALE COULD TOP 80 MLN STG
Britain's largest unquoted restaurant chain, Brightreasons is up for sale. The group that includes Pizzaland, Bella Pasta and Pizza Piazza, has 180 outlets and could fetch more than 80 million stg.
-- BIOTECH BOSS JOINS IN RACE FOR CAR FIRM

Biotech entrepreneur Chris Evans has made an 11th-hour offer for UK sports car group Lotus. The offer is believed to be much less than the 50 million stg bid from Daewoo for 100 percent of the company. It is thought that the move from Evans could be the reason why Daewoo's bid failed last week.
